detail:
Decisions: Chose to sort a copy of scoredItems by score before the presentation loop rather than re-merging the already-sorted warnings and nonWarnings arrays — the loop also populates open_needs, recent_findings, active_warnings and recent_questions, so one sorted iteration fixes every section's order consistently instead of only the decisions tier; Chose degrade-to-summary-only for warnings that exceed the token budget, rather than only counting the drops — a counter still loses the warning text entirely, whereas a 200-char summary costs ~50 tokens and preserves the actionable part; only warnings that cannot fit even as a summary increment warnings_omitted; Chose to compute resolved ids from the full live board rather than the scope slice, and to delete resolved obligations before scoring rather than hiding them at render — the resolving entry is frequently posted against a different scope, and filtering at render would leave resolved items consuming budget that live ones need; Chose to omit RecordSyncManager entirely when export_records is false rather than threading a flag into it — recordSync is already optional in StoreSet and every consumer guards on it, so not constructing it removes the destructive HEAD-move re-ingest path with no new branching; Chose to widen why()'s exclusion to a WHY_RETIRED_STATUSES set covering superseded, overridden and archived rather than adding 'overridden' alone — archived is equally non-authoritative and was missing from both the filter and WHY_STATUS_RANK, so adding only the reported status would have left the same class of bug in place; Chose to keep the existing superseded_count field name while widening what it counts, rather than adding a separate retired_count — avoids a breaking change to the why() response shape for a count that is only ever displayed as 'N more retired decisions'
Findings: All 6 regression tests were verified to FAIL against the unfixed code by stashing src/ and re-running — a test that passes without the fix pins nothing. The first version of the ordering test DID pass unfixed because the fixture's store order coincidentally matched score order; it was rewritten around confidence (an insertion-order-independent scoring input) until it discriminated. This is the same weakness the verifier identified in decision-propagation.test.ts:155.; warning: The full suite was green for the entire time all 6 of these defects were live (1452 tests). Test count is not evidence of retrieval correctness — nothing asserted presentation order, resolution filtering, or budget-drop behavior before this.; The two 'critical' findings were downgraded to high by adversarial verifiers on the grounds that archived entries remain recoverable from .twining/archive/*.jsonl and git history — the loss is silent removal from every live retrieval surface, not permanent destruction.; need: archiver.ts:50 cutoff=now and pre-commit-hook.sh:38 compound-command bypass are both confirmed high severity but carry medium fix risk and were NOT fixed — the archiver fix needs a count-based retention policy (an age cutoff alone still fully sweeps a same-hour burst of 500 entries) plus a new config field, and the hook fix needs clause-splitting on &&/||/;/|/newlines.
summary: Fixed 6 confirmed high-severity defects: assemble ordering, resolved-obligation leak, silent warning drop, why() retired statuses, ingest data loss, reverse-migrate wipe
